JOINT APPLICATION OF ONCOR                                    §

AND LCRA TRANSMISSION SERVICE                                 §
CORPORATION TO AMEND THEIR                                    §   OF
CERTIFICATES OF CONVENIENCE                                   §

COUNTY EAST SWITCH TO BIG HILL                                §
SUBSTATION 765-KV TRANSMISSION                                §
LINE PROJECT                                                  §



                         POST HEARING BRIEF OF
        ALBERT L. ANDERSON FAMILY LIMITED PARTNERSHIP (PARTY 596)


         The Albert L. Anderson Family Limited Partnership (“Intervenor” or “the Partnership”)

files this Post Hearing Brief in support of its position that the Commission should not select any

route that includes Link M8.

                                         I.       INTRODUCTION

         The Partnership opposes a single link – Link M8 – and asks the Commission to select any

of the many filed routes that avoid it. It asks the Commission to do precisely what both the

Applicants and Commission Staff have already done: route this line without Link M8.

         That is the decisive fact of this case. The Applicants identified Route 894 as the route that

best meets the requirements of PURA and the Commission’s rules. 1 Staff identified Route 487.2

Neither route uses Link M8. When asked whether Link M8 was included on any best-meets route,

the Applicants’ own routing witness confirmed it did not. 3 Of the 122 filed routes, only four,



1
  Direct Testimony of Casey Petty at 11–12 (Route 894 identified as the route that best meets the applicable routing
factors); Rebuttal Testimony of Casey Petty at 4–5 (same);
2
  Direct Testimony of John Poole at 29–30 (Staff recommending Route 487).
3
  Hr’g Tr. 105:7–9, June 9, 2026 (Perkins) (“And Link M8 was not included on any best meets route? — That is
correct.”).


4897-5871-4549
 Routes 304, 739, 910, and 911, contain Link M8; the other 118 avoid it entirely, including both

best-meets routes. 4 Rejecting M8, therefore, costs the project nothing. The relief the Partnership

seeks is already embedded in the recommendations of the only two parties advocating a “best

meets” route.

        The Applicants’ own Environmental Assessment establishes the rest. By the Applicants’

own data, M8 is among the most impactful links in the entire 15-county study area: it carries the

highest concentration of habitable structures in the Menard County corridor, it abuts the closest

Official Texas Historical Marker to any link in the filing, and it parallels a state highway rather

than a utility corridor – a routing choice that concentrates avoidable harm. And the Applicants

never analyzed it, never surveyed it, and never consulted the Texas Historical Commission about

it. On this record, the Applicants have not carried their burden as to Link M8, and the factors the

Commission must weigh point decisively away from it.

                             II.      ARGUMENTS AND AUTHORITIES

      A.      The Commission must select the route that best meets the statutory factors —
not merely a compliant one.

        Under PURA § 37.056(c)(4)(A)–(D) and 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B), the Commission must

weigh, among other things, community values, recreational and park areas, historical and aesthetic

values, environmental integrity, and the Commission’s policy of prudent avoidance. 5 The burden

rests on the Applicants, as the parties seeking the certificate, to demonstrate that the route they

seek satisfies those criteria.


4
  Of the 122 filed routes, only Routes 304, 739, 910, and 911 contain Link M8, confirmed by cross-referencing the
link compositions in EA App. D, Table 7-1 against the filed routes listed by corridor in Direct Testimony of Casey
Petty, Ex. CDP-6 (122 filed routes across five geographic corridors). Neither best-meets route includes M8: Route
894 (Direct Testimony of Casey Petty at 12 (link composition)) and Route 487 (Direct Testimony of John Poole at
29–30).
5
  PURA § 37.056(c)(4)(A)–(D); 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B); see also Direct Testimony of Russell J. Marusak at 20–
21 (routing evaluated under these provisions and the policy of prudent avoidance); Direct Testimony of John Poole at
29.

                                                         2
          Statutory compliance is the floor, not the test. The contention that Applicants’ 122 filed

routes “comply” with PURA and the rules addresses the wrong question. As the Applicants’ own

witness agreed on cross, “the Commission’s task here is to select the route that best meets the

statutory factors, not just merely one that is compliant.” 6 That concession frames the entire case:

the question is not whether a route containing Link M8 could lawfully be built, but whether M8

belongs in the route that best serves the statutory factors. On the proponents’ own analysis, it does

not.

         B.       The Applicants’ own evidence condemns Link M8.

         Every fact below comes from the Applicants’ Environmental Assessment and supporting

appendices — not from the Partnership.

    •    Residential concentration. Link M8 has 13 habitable structures within 500 feet of its
         centerline — the highest count of any link in the Menard County corridor — including a
         single-family residence just 95 feet from the centerline. 7
    •    Cultural and historical resources. The Pegleg Crossing on the San Saba Official Texas
         Historical Marker sits just 110 feet from the M8 centerline, on Intervenor’s property. The
         EA identifies only five Official Texas Historical Markers within 1,000 feet of any link
         across the entire 15-county study area — and at 110 feet, M8’s is the closest of them all.
         Darley Infant Cemetery lies 565 feet from the centerline. 8
    •    Highway paralleling, not utility paralleling. Link M8 parallels approximately 7.5 miles
         (39,463 feet) of State Highway 29 but only about 0.8 mile (4,344 feet) of existing
         transmission line. The Commission’s criteria favor paralleling existing compatible utility
         rights-of-way; M8 was instead drawn to follow a highway, which concentrates the line
         through the densely parceled corridor where structures cluster. 9



6
  Hr’g Tr. 105:3–6, June 9, 2026 (Perkins) (agreeing the Commission’s task is to select the route that best meets the
statutory factors, “not just merely one that is compliant”).
7
  Direct Testimony of DeAnn Dungan at 4 (13 habitable structures within 500 feet of the M8 centerline; single-family
residence 95 feet from the centerline); Partnership Statement of Position at 8; see also Direct Testimony of Russell J.
Marusak at 20 (habitable structures within 500 feet tabulated in the EA); EA App. E.
8
  Direct Testimony of DeAnn Dungan at 7–8; Partnership Statement of Position at 6; EA App. F, Table 7-9 & Fig. 3-
1F (Official Texas Historical Markers within 1,000 feet of any link).
9
  Partnership Statement of Position at 2 (39,463 feet / approx. 7.5 miles paralleling State Highway 29; 4,344 feet
paralleling existing transmission line); Direct Testimony of DeAnn Dungan at 12; EA App. E, Table 7-3.

                                                          3
      •   Watershed and endangered species. Link M8 crosses 4.8 miles of riparian areas and 18
         stream crossings draining into the San Saba River — federally designated critical habitat
         for the Texas fatmucket and Texas pimpleback mussels. 10

         C.      Link M8 is an outlier, and it was added without analysis or public input.

         M8 is not a representative link – it is a statistical outlier that the Applicants added late in

the process. The links into which the former M3 corridor was divided, M32 and M33, carry just

one habitable structure between them; M8 carries thirteen. 11 And M8 was conceived after the June

2025 public participation meetings, as the Applicants’ environmental witness confirmed, and was

added by the EA’s own account to parallel State Highway 29. 12 The landowners along the Highway

29 corridor near Hext, the people most affected by M8, had no opportunity to be heard on this link

during the formal public-involvement process. 13

         The Partnership does not contend the Applicants’ notice was unlawful. It contends, more

simply, that a link generated after the public meetings, never tested against the corridor it

supplements, and never the subject of public comment is entitled to less weight under the

community-values factor – not more – when it concentrates impacts no other Menard County link

approaches.

       D.     No route that “best meets” the factors includes Link M8 and avoiding M8
requires no exotic route.




10
   Direct Testimony of DeAnn Dungan at 10; Partnership Statement of Position at 4-5; EA Table 7-4 & App. E–F
(riparian areas, stream crossings, and San Saba River critical habitat for the Texas fatmucket and Texas pimpleback).
11
   Partnership Statement of Position at 8 (Links M32 and M33 carry one habitable structure total, compared with
thirteen on M8 alone); EA Table 6-1 at 6-25 (addition of Link M8 split Link M3 into M32 and M33, and Link P4 into
P41 and P42).
12
    Hr’g Tr. 103:10–12, June 9, 2026 (Marusak confirming Link M8 was conceived after the June 2025 public
meetings); EA § 6.1, Table 6-1 at 6-26 (Link M8 “added to consider an alternative that parallels State Highway 29”);
see also Direct Testimony of DeAnn Dungan at 4, 12.
13
   Direct Testimony of Russell J. Marusak at 15 (public participation meetings held June 16–18, 2025); cf. Hr’g Tr.
60:13–61:5, June 8, 2026 (Perkins) (owners within 520 feet of a post-meeting link did not receive direct-mail notice
of the June 2025 meetings); Rebuttal Testimony of Casey Petty at 7 (no additional public meeting held for landowners
affected by added or modified links).

                                                         4
          The Applicants recommend Route 894. Staff recommends Route 487. Neither contains

Link M8. 14 The Applicants’ witness confirmed on cross that M8 appears on no best-meets route. 15

Of the 122 filed routes, only four, Routes 304, 739, 910, and 911, include M8; the remaining 118

– including both best-meets routes – avoid it entirely. 16

         The Partnership therefore asks for nothing unusual. The relief it seeks is achievable using

the Applicants’ own recommended route, Staff’s recommended route, or any of the scores of other

filed routes the Applicants have already judged feasible. When the proponents’ holistic balancing

has already excluded M8 from every route either of them recommends, the Commission can

decline M8 with full confidence that doing so sacrifices nothing the record supports.

         The Applicants will respond that the Commission selects whole routes endpoint-to-

endpoint, not individual links, and does not route around a single landowner. And that is precisely

why the Partnership asks the Commission to select a whole route, not to excise a link. The

endpoint-to-endpoint exercise the Applicants describe has already been performed twice, once by

the Applicants and once by Staff, and both times it produced a complete, constructible route that

excludes M8. Declining M8 thus demands no link-surgery and no departure from the

Commission’s ordinary practice; it requires only that the Commission adopt one of the many entire

routes that already avoid it. 17

         That convergence is itself probative. Staff’s witness agreed that a corridor that remains

preferred regardless of how the statutory factors are weighted is more robust than one that depends


14
   Hr’g Tr. 105:7–9, June 9, 2026 (Perkins); Direct Testimony of Casey Petty at 12 (Route 894 link composition,
omitting M8); Direct Testimony of John Poole at 29–30 (Route 487).
15
   Hr’g Tr. 105:7–9, June 9, 2026 (Perkins).
16
   See supra note 4 (four filed routes contain M8; neither best-meets route does). Two of the four are themselves
outliers: Route 910 is the longest filed route (244.4 miles) and the most expensive (Direct Testimony of Casey Petty,
Ex. CDP-6). See also Rebuttal Testimony of Casey Petty at 5 (all filed routes viable and constructible).
17
   Hr’g Tr. 164:20–165:6, June 9, 2026 (Perkins) (routes evaluated endpoint-to-endpoint, not by the impacts on a
single landowner).

 on a single analyst’s undocumented judgment. 18 Here, the avoidance of M8 is the rare point on

which the Applicants and Staff agree — their two independently derived best-meets routes diverge

on much, but both exclude Link M8.

       E.     The Applicants did not carry their burden as to Link M8, and their analytical
gaps are construed against them.

         Even setting aside the best-meets concession, the Applicants’ evidentiary support for M8

is hollow. Their environmental witness admitted that the Applicants conducted no survey or

fieldwork at the Pegleg Crossing, undertook no consultation with the Texas Historical Commission

specific to M8, and intend to defer any such consultation until after a route is approved. 19 A cultural

resource of the significance the EA itself flags should not be evaluated for the first time after the

Commission has already committed the line to its doorstep.

         The aesthetic record is no better. Staff’s witness, Mr. Poole, conceded that the application

contains no quantified visual-impact analysis under the Bureau of Land Management’s visual

resource management system or any other recognized methodology — and that his own aesthetic

findings rest on the qualifier “potentially.” 20 He further conceded that his route selection reflects

unweighted, undocumented professional judgment that an independent reviewer cannot reproduce,

which is why he and the Applicants, looking at the same data, reached different routes. 21 Where

the proponents’ visual and cultural analysis is admittedly incomplete, the resulting gaps are




18
   Hr’g Tr. 157:3–18, June 10, 2026 (Poole) (a route that remains preferred regardless of how the factors are weighted
is more robust, and such convergence gives the Commission greater confidence).
19

Commission consultation specific to Link M8; any consultation deferred until after a route is approved).
20

impact analysis under the Bureau of Land Management’s visual resource management system or any other recognized
methodology).
21

independently reproducible; two qualified engineers applying the same factors reached different routes — Staff’s 487
and Applicants’ 894); Direct Testimony of John Poole at 29.

 construed against the party bearing the burden of proof, the Applicants, not against the landowner

who would absorb the consequences.

         F.       Prudent avoidance and community values both point away from Link M8.

         The Commission’s policy of prudent avoidance calls for limiting exposures that can be

avoided through reasonable investments of money and effort. 22 The defining feature of this case

is that avoiding M8 requires no meaningful investment at all – the line need only follow one of the

many routes the Applicants and Staff already endorse. When avoidance is essentially free, prudent

avoidance is not a close call.

         The community values, historical, and aesthetic factors reinforce the result. Intervenor’s

property encompasses Pegleg Crossing on the San Saba, a site whose documented history spans

Spanish colonial exploration, a 1732 Spanish-Apache battle, a military ford, the Pegleg stagecoach

station and its notorious robberies, the Great Western Cattle Trail, and a celebrated chapter of

Texas Ranger history, all commemorated by an Official Texas Historical Marker erected by the

Texas Historical Commission. 23 A 200-foot lattice tower 110 feet away would render that

landscape unrecognizable from the scene the marker exists to interpret. And the Applicants’ own

environmental witness, Russell Marusak, agreed that avoiding the bisection and fragmentation of

property is a routing criterion, grounded in Commission Substantive Rule 25.101(b)(3)(B), and

that bisecting land is intrusive and can render a property less usable. 24 M8 runs counter to those

principles.



22
   16 TAC § 25.101 (prudent avoidance is the limiting of exposures that can be avoided with reasonable investments
of money and effort); Direct Testimony of Casey Petty at 15 (quoting the rule’s definition); Direct Testimony of
Russell J. Marusak at 20–21.
23
   Direct Testimony of DeAnn Dungan at 7-10.
24
   Hr’g Tr. 170:14–172:2, June 8, 2026 (Marusak) (Applicants try to avoid bisecting property; “paralleling property
boundaries” is a routing criterion; bisecting and fragmentation are intrusive and can render a property less usable; the
relevant authority is Substantive Rule 25.101(b)(3)(B)); see also Hr’g Tr. 127:1–127:11, June 9, 2026 (Marusak
agreeing, as to land use and landowner values).

                                                           7
                                III.    CONCLUSION AND PRAYER

        This is not a case in which an intervenor asks the Commission to disrupt a carefully

balanced route to spare one property. It is a case in which the link the Partnership opposes has

already been rejected by everyone who has recommended a route — the Applicants and Staff

alike. 25 The Applicants’ own data show M8 to be an outlier on residential concentration, on

cultural-resource proximity, and on highway-versus-utility paralleling, and the Applicants admit

they never analyzed, surveyed, or consulted on it. The factors the Commission must weigh, and

the recommendations of the only parties advocating a best-meets route, converge on a single

conclusion: this line should be built without Link M8. Accordingly, the Partnership respectfully

requests that the Commission select a route that avoids Link M8 — including the Applicants’

recommended Route 894, Staff’s recommended Route 487, or any other filed route that excludes

Link M8.

         F.       Prudent avoidance and community values both point away from Link M8.

         The Commission's policy of prudent avoidance calls for limiting exposures that can be

avoided through reasonable investments of money and effort.22 The defining feature of this case

is that avoiding M8 requires no meaningful investment at all - the line need only follow one of the

many routes the Applicants and Staff already endorse. When avoidance is essentially free, prudent

avoidance is not a close call.

         The community values, historical, and aesthetic factors reinforce the result. Intervenor' s

property encompasses Pegleg Crossing on the San Saba, a site whose documented history spans

Spanish colonial exploration, a 1732 Spanish-Apache battle, a military ford, the Pegleg stagecoach

station and its notorious robberies, the Great Western Cattle Trail, and a celebrated chapter of

Texas Ranger history, all commemorated by an Official Texas Historical Marker erected by the

Texas Historical Commission.23 A 200-foot lattice tower 110 feet away would render that

landscape unrecognizable from the scene the marker exists to interpret. And the Applicants' own

environmental witness, Russell Marusak, agreed that avoiding the bisection and fragmentation of

property is a routing criterion, grounded in Commission Substantive Rule 25.101(b)(3)(B), and

that bisecting land is intrusive and can render a property less usable.24 M8 runs counter to those

principles.

                                III.    CONCLUSION AND PRAYER

        This is not a case in which an intervenor asks the Commission to disrupt a carefully

balanced route to spare one property. It is a case in which the link the Partnership opposes has

already been rej ected by everyone who has recommended a route - the Applicants and Staff

alike.25 The Applicants' own data show M8 to be an outlier on residential concentration, on

cultural-resource proximity, and on highway-versus-utility paralleling, and the Applicants admit

they never analyzed, surveyed, or consulted on it. The factors the Commission must weigh, and

the recommendations of the only parties advocating a best-meets route, converge on a single

conclusion: this line should be built without Link M8. Accordingly, the Partnership respectfully

requests that the Commission select a route that avoids Link M8 - including the Applicants'

recommended Route 894, Staff' s recommended Route 487, or any other filed route that excludes

Link M8.
